currentContext.business: Established in 1987 and headquartered in Noida, GFL operates integrated manufacturing facilities in Gujarat supported by a captive fluorspar mine in Morocco that secures a stable supply of critical raw materials. Its portfolio spans high-performance fluoropolymers such as PTFE, PVDF, FKM and FFKM, alongside fluoro-specialty chemicals, refrigerants and industrial chemicals, serving pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and automotive customers. Over recent years it has moved from a traditional fluorochemicals manufacturer towards an innovation-led solutions provider, building capabilities in EV battery materials, BESS, semiconductors and renewables through subsidiaries such as GFCL EV Products Limited and GFCL Solar and Green Hydrogen Products Limited.

currentContext.strengths: Integrated manufacturing ecosystem connecting multiple stages of the fluorochemical value chain (fluorspar - hydrofluoric acid - monomers - fluoropolymers / refrigerants / battery materials) into a unified operating platform|Backward integration: a large proportion of critical raw materials produced in-house, with little dependence on external markets beyond commodity inputs such as coal and salt, giving control over raw material availability, quality and cost|Captive fluorspar mining and beneficiation in Morocco securing a stable supply of a critical raw material|Scale leadership in India - largest refrigerant capacity (Ranjitnagar) and largest fluoropolymer plant (Dahej) in India, as stated in the report|Among a limited number of integrated non-Chinese producers of LiPF6 globally, with an LFP cathode active material plant among the first outside China by a non-Chinese player|Intellectual property base of 78 total active patents (including applications), with 26 applications filed and 5 granted in FY 2025-26|Diverse product profile serving a wide gamut of sectors including pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and automotive, with an expanding footprint across India, Europe and the United States|Globally recognised quality, environment, safety and automotive certifications across manufacturing sites
currentContext.strategies: Leadership development is stated as a cornerstone of the Company's long-term growth strategy, run through the LEAP programme (Learn, Elevate, Accelerate, Pioneer) to identify, nurture and prepare high-potential employees for future leadership responsibilities and to build a sustainable internal talent pipeline.|Structured talent-acceleration and ownership programmes were rolled out during the year - Aarohan for L5-level employees at the Dahej B unit in January 2026, and Kartavyam for L5(S) and L6 employees at the Ranjitnagar unit - to strengthen capability, ownership and accountability.|Stated way forward is to continue leadership development initiatives that build managerial effectiveness, strengthen succession pipelines and prepare future leaders.
currentContext.expansion: GFL's manufacturing backbone is built on integrated facilities in Gujarat - Ranjitnagar (refrigerants and specialty chemicals, commissioned 1989), Dahej (fluoropolymers, specialty and bulk chemicals, commissioned 2007) and Jolva (fluoropolymers, specialty and new-age chemicals, under phased commissioning) - supported by captive fluorspar mining and beneficiation in Morocco. The stated key manufacturing footprint adds another new site at Dahej, another site in Oman for the EV business and a planned HFC blending facility in Dubai, taking the group to five manufacturing plants including subsidiary companies. During the year the Company commissioned additional R-32 production capacity at the existing refrigerants facility, commissioned Vinylene Carbonate (VC) and Fluoroethylene Carbonate (FEC) facilities at Ranjitnagar with customer samples already supplied for qualification, and achieved 3ABTF production of 100 MT per month. The Fluorochemicals segment commenced R32 production and sales in March 2026 and continues incremental capacity expansions to maximise utilisation of its production entitlements under the Kigali Amendment. In battery chemicals, GFL announced a US$ 216 Million greenfield battery materials project in Oman positioned to leverage US-India Free Trade Agreements, with PVDF binders in advanced qualification and commercial operations expected in the first half of FY 2026-27. Investment is directed at debottlenecking, capacity expansion, process optimisation and selective retrofitting so existing assets can carry new chemistries, with the stated aim of raising the contribution of fluoropolymers and battery materials without compromising the efficiency of refrigerants and bulk chemicals. Capex plans of about Rs 3,150 Crores are stated in the Manufactured Capital section.

risks.risk: Process safety and contractor safety management
risks.note: Chemical processing and handling involve inherent risks of accidental releases, fires, explosions and exposure to hazardous substances; deficiencies in process safety systems or contractor safety practices may result in major operational incidents, injuries or regulatory non-compliance, with costs from remediation, asset damage, regulatory action and business interruption. Mitigated through PSM, HAZOP/PHA studies, permit-to-work, pre-startup safety reviews and audits.

Intensifying competition and pricing pressures may adversely affect revenue realisation, profitability and market share; the response is a focus on value-added products, product-mix optimisation, cost competitiveness and pricing discipline.

risks.risk: Product portfolio obsolescence and regulatory transition
risks.note: Evolving regulations and changing customer preferences may reduce demand for existing products and accelerate the need for portfolio transformation, requiring continuous regulatory monitoring, accelerated product innovation and investment in next-generation fluorochemicals and advanced materials.

risks.risk: Asset integrity and ageing critical equipment and infrastructure
risks.note: Ageing assets, inadequate condition monitoring and maintenance gaps may impact plant reliability, operational continuity and safety; mitigation relies on preventive and predictive maintenance, expanded asset condition monitoring, reliability improvements, RCA and lifecycle planning for critical equipment.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity exposure across OT/ICS and information/IP leakage
risks.note: Legacy operational technology and industrial control systems increase vulnerability to cyberattacks that could disrupt manufacturing; separately, weak information governance and unauthorised use of external AI and digital platforms may expose confidential business information, intellectual property and personal data.

risks.risk: Climate change, carbon costs and the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
risks.note: Climate change presents risks through evolving regulations, carbon-related costs, changing customer expectations and the need to decarbonise energy-intensive operations across GFL's operations and value chain; increasing carbon disclosure requirements under CBAM are flagged as a separate key risk, with potential increases in operating, compliance and transition costs.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance and timely statutory filing
risks.note: Weak compliance tracking and delayed statutory filings may result in regulatory penalties, business disruptions and reputational damage; managed via a digital compliance management platform with automated alerts, defined ownership, periodic reviews, escalation and internal audits.

risks.risk: Water availability, effluent discharge and hazardous waste / resource use
risks.note: Water availability and wastewater management present risks to regulatory compliance, resource availability and operational continuity, while resource consumption and hazardous waste generation increase environmental exposure, disposal costs and regulatory risk - both feed directly into operating cost and licence to operate at the Ranjitnagar, Dahej and Jolva sites.

Inadequate insurance coverage may expose the Company to financial losses arising from operational disruptions or unforeseen events; mitigation is periodic adequacy review, a centralised insurance register, reinstatement value assessment and claims monitoring.

one-line thesis: Gujarat Fluorochemicals Ltd is a leading specialty chemicals company with a strong market position in fluoropolymers and fluorochemicals, and is well-positioned to benefit from growing demand in electric vehicle batteries and renewable energy. The company has a diversified product portfolio and a strong financial risk profile, with a healthy operating margin and robust debt protection metrics. However, the company's performance is susceptible to fluctuations in global supply and prices, especially in bulk chemicals and refrigerant gases.
financial scorecard / credit view: Revenue: Rs 3,628 crore (9M FY26), EBITDA: Rs 981 crore (9M FY26), PAT: Rs 546 crore (FY25), Net Debt: Rs 1,532 crore (Dec 2025), Credit Rating: CRISIL AA+/Stable
guidance / outlook: The company expects to maintain a healthy operating margin and robust debt protection metrics, driven by growing demand in electric vehicle batteries and renewable energy. The company plans to invest Rs 1,700 crore per annum in the new fluoropolymer segment, including battery chemicals, over the next few fiscals.
segment / subsidiary detail: Fluoropolymers: 60% of revenue (FY25), Fluorochemicals: 40% of revenue (FY25)
growth verticals / optionality: Growing demand in electric vehicle batteries and renewable energy, expansion into new fluoropolymer products
margins & cost dynamics: Operating margin: 27% (9M FY26), EBITDA margin: 25-27% (expected over the medium term)
capex / expansion: Rs 1,700 crore per annum (planned for the next few fiscals)
capital allocation: The company plans to fund its capex through internal accrual and equity infusion, with a focus on maintaining a healthy financial risk profile.
risks & watch-items: Fluctuations in global supply and prices, especially in bulk chemicals and refrigerant gases, production quota restrictions, and foreign exchange risks
non-obvious takeaways: The company's move towards R-32 production to mitigate the risk of production quota restrictions in the fluorochemicals business

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1987 and headquartered in Noida, GFL operates integrated manufacturing facilities in Gujarat supported by a captive fluorspar mine in Morocco that secures a stable supply of critical raw materials. Its portfolio spans high-performance fluoropolymers such as PTFE, PVDF, FKM and FFKM, alongside fluoro-specialty chemicals, refrigerants and industrial chemicals, serving pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and automotive customers. Over recent years it has moved from a traditional fluorochemicals manufacturer towards an innovation-led solutions provider, building capabilities in EV battery materials, BESS, semiconductors and renewables through subsidiaries such as GFCL EV Products Limited and GFCL Solar and Green Hydrogen Products Limited.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Fluoropolymers are positioned as the backbone of next-generation technologies, with the global fluoropolymer market estimated to reach US$ 19.3 Billion by 2035.
- Electric mobility, semiconductors, solar energy, green hydrogen, space exploration and artificial intelligence are named as the principal growth engines for the fluoropolymer industry, collectively representing a US$ 5 Trillion opportunity by 2035.
- The fluoropolymers market is transitioning from material substitution to performance-driven demand, with growing reliance on custom-engineered formulations to meet specific thermal, mechanical and chemical requirements.
- Cost structures remain closely linked to monomer availability, processing complexity and stringent quality control standards, which has led to margin concentration among established players with integrated production capabilities and global distribution networks.
- Competitive advantage is increasingly defined by control over high-performance resin production, formulation expertise and the ability to ensure consistent quality at scale, while smaller entrants focus on niche segments.
- Demand drivers cited: rising need for high-performance materials, product innovation, the shift to sustainable and eco-friendly alternatives, expansion of renewable energy and green technologies, Asia-Pacific and emerging-market industrialisation, 5G and IoT infrastructure, and rising demand from Global Capability Centres.
- End-market anchors quantified by the report: electric mobility to reach a US$ 135 Billion market size by 2030, semiconductors to achieve a US$ 1 Trillion market by 2030, solar energy to achieve 3 TW installed capacity by 2030, and green hydrogen to reach 38 MTPA clean hydrogen production by 2030.
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP expansion is projected at 6.8-7.2% in FY 2026-27, supported by robust consumption in semi-urban and rural areas, improving investment intentions, healthier household and corporate balance sheets and sustained public spending in infrastructure.
- Stated external risks to the outlook: slower growth in key trading partners, evolving trade policies, periodic financial market volatility, and energy prices expected to remain volatile with a sharp decline unlikely.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: GFL's manufacturing backbone is built on integrated facilities in Gujarat - Ranjitnagar (refrigerants and specialty chemicals, commissioned 1989), Dahej (fluoropolymers, specialty and bulk chemicals, commissioned 2007) and Jolva (fluoropolymers, specialty and new-age chemicals, under phased commissioning) - supported by captive fluorspar mining and beneficiation in Morocco. The stated key manufacturing footprint adds another new site at Dahej, another site in Oman for the EV business and a planned HFC blending facility in Dubai, taking the group to five manufacturing plants including subsidiary companies. During the year the Company commissioned additional R-32 production capacity at the existing refrigerants facility, commissioned Vinylene Carbonate (VC) and Fluoroethylene Carbonate (FEC) facilities at Ranjitnagar with customer samples already supplied for qualification, and achieved 3ABTF production of 100 MT per month. The Fluorochemicals segment commenced R32 production and sales in March 2026 and continues incremental capacity expansions to maximise utilisation of its production entitlements under the Kigali Amendment. In battery chemicals, GFL announced a US$ 216 Million greenfield battery materials project in Oman positioned to leverage US-India Free Trade Agreements, with PVDF binders in advanced qualification and commercial operations expected in the first half of FY 2026-27. Investment is directed at debottlenecking, capacity expansion, process optimisation and selective retrofitting so existing assets can carry new chemistries, with the stated aim of raising the contribution of fluoropolymers and battery materials without compromising the efficiency of refrigerants and bulk chemicals. Capex plans of about Rs 3,150 Crores are stated in the Manufactured Capital section.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated manufacturing ecosystem connecting multiple stages of the fluorochemical value chain (fluorspar - hydrofluoric acid - monomers - fluoropolymers / refrigerants / battery materials) into a unified operating platform
- Backward integration: a large proportion of critical raw materials produced in-house, with little dependence on external markets beyond commodity inputs such as coal and salt, giving control over raw material availability, quality and cost
- Captive fluorspar mining and beneficiation in Morocco securing a stable supply of a critical raw material
- Scale leadership in India - largest refrigerant capacity (Ranjitnagar) and largest fluoropolymer plant (Dahej) in India, as stated in the report
- Among a limited number of integrated non-Chinese producers of LiPF6 globally, with an LFP cathode active material plant among the first outside China by a non-Chinese player
- Intellectual property base of 78 total active patents (including applications), with 26 applications filed and 5 granted in FY 2025-26
- Diverse product profile serving a wide gamut of sectors including pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and automotive, with an expanding footprint across India, Europe and the United States
- Globally recognised quality, environment, safety and automotive certifications across manufacturing sites

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Fluctuations in global supply and prices, especially in bulk chemicals and refrigerant gases, production quota restrictions, and foreign exchange risks

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The company's move towards R-32 production to mitigate the risk of production quota restrictions in the fluorochemicals business

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Leadership development is stated as a cornerstone of the Company's long-term growth strategy, run through the LEAP programme (Learn, Elevate, Accelerate, Pioneer) to identify, nurture and prepare high-potential employees for future leadership responsibilities and to build a sustainable internal talent pipeline.
- Structured talent-acceleration and ownership programmes were rolled out during the year - Aarohan for L5-level employees at the Dahej B unit in January 2026, and Kartavyam for L5(S) and L6 employees at the Ranjitnagar unit - to strengthen capability, ownership and …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group structure] GFCL EV is a battery-materials subsidiary of GFL catering to the EV/ESS ecosystem through battery salts, additives, electrolytes, CAM, cathode binders and NGAAM (anode); a separate GFL subsidiary serves the solar and green hydrogen value chain.
- [Market outlook] Ex-China Li-ion cell demand outlook shown as ~500 GWh in CY26 to ~1.8 TWh in CY30 at a ~38% implied CAGR, with LFP expected "to remain the dominant chemistry across mass-market EV & ESS" and AI/data-centre-driven electricity demand cited as a BESS driver.
- [Segment outlook] Refrigerants "demand and pricing remain stable in near term"; caustic soda demand "expected to remain stable in FY27"; "Chloromethanes performance is likely to remain range bound"; fluoropolymer "Demand momentum expected to remain healthy".
- [Supply chain] "Supply-chain localization remains a key tailwind, as customers increasingly prioritize supply security and diversified sourcing, supporting our strategic positioning."
- [Labour code] Q4FY26 PAT is stated before an exceptional item related to implementation of the new labour code of Rs. 2 crore (net of tax) in the Chemical Segment and Rs. 3 crore (net of tax) in Consolidated.
